severities.label: Important
severities.description: Serious bug or weakness without immediate exploitation

releases.title: Messages start at the margin, their time at the end
releases.summary: On every platform a message starts at the margin, with no column of times before it, and its time stands at the end of its last line; group messages from history no longer say the sender is not verified. On Android your video keeps its picture while it goes, and on Android and the desktop a file its sender cancelled says so. Android and the desktop get 0.2.80; the iPhone gets TestFlight build 143018 (1.4.34).

changes.title: Messages start at the margin, their time at the end
changes.description: A message no longer starts after a column of times: it starts at the margin, in a group after the tile of its author. Its time, the word edited and the mark of a message of yours stand at the end of its last line, or on a line of their own under it when that line is full; files, voice messages, photos and calls keep theirs at the bottom, at the far edge. Group messages that came from the history of other members no longer carry the yellow line Received from history, sender not verified: they look as any other message, with the tile of their author, which opens that member. Each paragraph keeps its own direction, so a paragraph of figures, such as a phone number or coordinates, reads left to right in an Arabic interface.

changes.title: Android: your video keeps its picture while it goes
changes.description: While a video of yours was being sent, its entry showed a paper clip in place of the video. It now shows the picture of the video, how much is left to send and Cancel, and a tap plays it.

changes.title: A file its sender cancelled says so
changes.description: When the sender cancelled a file before it was whole, the person it went to read The download stopped and could not tell why, or whether anything on their side would bring it back. The entry now says The sender cancelled it, in the muted colour and without Retry. On Android it keeps saying so after a restart; on the desktop until the app is closed.

changes.title: Desktop: a sample of the smiley set
changes.description: Under the smiley set in Settings, Chats, a few emoticons stand as a message shows them with that set, at the size chosen, so the sets can be told apart: the ASCII sets leave typed smileys as text, Classic has pictures of its own, and emojione and Universe are drawn differently.

changes.title: A shorter line for the founder of a group
changes.description: In the group's details, Your role reads You founded the group. You manage its members, moderators and settings.

releases.title: A message no longer brings up a hidden window
releases.summary: On the desktop a message no longer brings up a window hidden in the tray: Open the window on a new message starts off for everyone, and turning it on again in Settings, Notifications is kept. The desktop gets 0.2.79; Android stays at 0.2.78 and the iPhone at TestFlight build 143017 (1.4.34).

changes.title: Desktop: a message no longer brings up a hidden window
changes.description: With the window hidden in the tray, every message showed it and made it the active one, in front of the work at hand: Open the window on a new message (Settings, Notifications) was on for everyone who had never turned it off. It now starts off for everyone, and turning it on again is kept. The system notification, the sign on the tray icon and the sound come as before.

releases.title: A shared place is where you are, on Android
releases.summary: On Android a shared place is where you are: the app sends the most accurate fresh fix of every location source that is on, and asks once for the exact place when only the approximate one is allowed. Quotes, the chat list and notifications call a place a location. Android gets 0.2.78; the desktop stays at 0.2.77 and the iPhone at TestFlight build 143017 (1.4.34).

changes.title: Android: a shared place is where you are
changes.description: A place shared from Android could be kilometres off: the app took the newest fix the phone had, from whichever source and however rough, and after 15 seconds without one it sent any fix at all, however old. It now listens to every location source that is on and sends the most accurate fresh fix: at once within 20 metres, within 65 metres after two and a half seconds, otherwise the best one when the 15 seconds end, or one the phone had in the last two minutes. With only the approximate location allowed (Android 12 and newer), a share asks once to allow the exact one; a no sends the approximate place, as allowed.

changes.title: Android: a place is called a location
changes.description: A reply to a place, the reply bar and TalkBack say Location and the coordinates, no longer the text khandaq-location:; the chat list, notifications and in-app bands say Location, and a reaction to a place says it was to your location.

releases.title: A shared place is a map on the desktop
releases.summary: On the desktop a place someone shares is a small map with a marker that opens on OpenStreetMap, no longer a line of letters and numbers, and quotes, the chat list and notifications call it a location. On the iPhone a shared place is where you are, with a pin on its map. The desktop gets 0.2.77 and the iPhone TestFlight build 143017 (1.4.34); Android stays at 0.2.75.

changes.title: Desktop: a shared place is a map
changes.description: A place shared from a phone showed on the desktop as the text khandaq-location: and its coordinates. It is now a map card: the map around the place with a marker on it, and under it Location and the coordinates; a click opens the place on openstreetmap.org. The map comes from OpenStreetMap through the proxy set in the app's settings, without cookies; while it loads, or when it cannot, the card keeps its place and tries again after a minute.

changes.title: iPhone: a shared place is where you are
changes.description: A place shared from the iPhone could be kilometres off, because the app asked for the reduced accuracy. It now waits up to 8 seconds for a fresh fix and sends the most accurate one; with Precise Location off for the app, it asks once for the exact place, and a share that gets no fix says so. The map in the chat has a pin on the place, with the coordinates as its caption; quotes, the chat list and notifications say Location, and holding a chat in the list shows its places, photos, videos and quotes as the chat does.

changes.title: Desktop: a place is called a location everywhere
changes.description: A reply to a place, the reply bar, search, export and the queue of unsent messages show Location and the coordinates; the chat list, notifications and in-app bands say Location, and a reaction to a place says it was to your location.

releases.title: A group keeps its new name, and the desktop follows the scale of Windows
releases.summary: On the iPhone a group renamed a second time keeps its new name after the app restarts, and holding a group in the chat list shows who wrote each message. On Windows the desktop app is drawn at the scale set in the display settings, 125 % included. The iPhone app gets TestFlight build 143015 (1.4.34) and the desktop gets 0.2.76; Android stays at 0.2.75.

changes.title: iPhone: a group keeps its new name after the app restarts
changes.description: A group renamed a second time had its first new name again once the app was restarted, as a tester found. The iPhone app changed a group's name and settings but did not save them with the profile, so the next start loaded the older save. A group's name, password, member limit, privacy, who may change the name, who may speak and the members' roles are now saved as soon as they change.

changes.title: Windows: the app follows the scale of the display settings
changes.description: On Windows at a scale of 125 % the desktop app was drawn as at 100 %, its text and icons small next to every other window, as a tester found, and at 150 % it was drawn as at 200 %. The toolkit the app is built on rounds a screen's scale to a whole number; the app now makes up the rest before its window opens, so it is drawn at 125 %, 150 % or 175 % as set, each screen at its own scale. If you raised the size in the app's settings to make up for it, set it back to 100 %. A window left at nearly the whole screen opens within the screen at its new scale.

changes.title: iPhone: holding a group in the list shows who wrote
changes.description: Holding a group in the chat list showed its last messages as a talk between two, without the names of those who wrote them, under a round picture unlike the group's in the list. The preview now shows the group as the group itself does: the author's name over each run of their messages, in their colour, their initials beside the last message of the run, and the group's notices in the middle. Its header has the picture of the row: the Khandaq Community logo, the group's or the person's initials, the person's photo, or the bookmark of Saved Messages.

releases.title: The first call goes through, and long messages open at once
releases.summary: On Android the first audio call after the app starts reaches the other side again, and a chat with a very long message opens without freezing. Only the Android app changes in this release: the iPhone app stays at 1.4.34 (143014) and the desktop at 0.2.73.

changes.title: Android: the first audio call after the app starts goes through
changes.description: The first audio call placed after the app started never reached the other side: the call screen showed Calling, but the call was never sent, and only the next call went through. An audio call has no camera to wait for, so the call began before its screen existed, and the first update of the screen's text stopped the call before it was sent. The screen's text now waits for the screen, and nothing on the screen can stop the call itself.

changes.title: Android: a chat with a very long message opens at once
changes.description: A chat with a very long message still froze for up to a second and a half as it opened, longer on a slow phone, up to the system's "isn't responding" dialog: everything the list does to a message's words costs as much as they are long. A message now shows at most its first 3,000 characters in the chat, cut at the end of a line or a word, and Read more under it opens the whole text in a reader that lays it out in pieces as you scroll. Copy there takes the whole text, and a search shows the part of the message around the match.

releases.title: Calls keep the microphone in the background
releases.summary: On Android 11 and newer the other side of a call keeps hearing you when the screen is locked or another app is open during the call. Only the Android app changes in this release: the iPhone app stays at 1.4.34 (143014) and the desktop at 0.2.73.

changes.title: Android: a call keeps its microphone in the background
changes.description: Since Android 11 an app gets the microphone in the background only through a foreground service of the microphone type. The call's service was a special use service only, so when the screen was locked or another app was opened during a call, the call recorded silence and the other side stopped hearing you, as testers wrote. The call's service now also runs as a microphone service from Android 11 on, once the microphone is allowed; if Android 14 refuses that type at the moment the call starts, the call goes on with the service it had before.

releases.title: Calls without echo, and video that holds on a mobile link
releases.summary: Calls: on Android the phone's own echo cancelling now runs on every call and the other side sees your camera again in a video call, and on Android and iPhone the video of a call follows what a mobile link carries instead of breaking into blocks. On Android a chat with a very long message opens without freezing. A group's name that members can change is called its name on every platform, and the desktop shows it as the group's title. The iPhone app gets TestFlight build 143014 (1.4.34); the desktop gets 0.2.73.

changes.title: Calls: echo cancelling on Android
changes.description: Testers heard themselves come back several times in a call. Android recorded calls in a low latency mode that turns the phone's own echo cancelling and noise suppression off, and pushed the microphone and the loudspeaker into clipping, an echo no canceller can take out. A call now records for voice communication on every route with the phone's processing on, without the extra gain on the microphone and the loudspeaker.

changes.title: Android: the other side sees you in a video call
changes.description: Since 0.2.70 the camera of a video call on Android never opened: its preview could start only once drawn, in a box that stayed hidden until the camera had opened. The box now shows from the start, the other side sees you, and an outgoing video call no longer waits 16 seconds before it rings.

changes.title: Video that holds on a mobile link
changes.description: The iPhone app asked its video encoder for a thousand times the rate it meant, so its video came out at the encoder's worst quality on every call; it now starts at 600 kbit/s and follows what the link lets through, between 150 and 1200. Android held its video at 1500 kbit/s at least at the default quality and let it climb to 2500 on a mobile network; it now goes down to 250 when the link loses and tops out at 1000 on mobile.

changes.title: Android: a chat with a very long message opens without freezing
changes.description: Android said that Khandaq was not responding in a chat with a long piece of code, as a tester found. The app looked for emoji in all of a long text, several times for each message and once for each typed character, and laid it out anew each time. It now looks only where emoji can be, sets a message's text once, and no longer lays out a long draft again for each key.

changes.title: Android: the screen stays on through a call
changes.description: On Android 8.1 and later only the call buttons kept the screen on, so with them hidden, in picture in picture, the screen could go off in the middle of a call. The call screen now keeps it on, as on older Android, and leaving the call screen no longer restarts the sound.

changes.title: A group has one name
changes.description: A group's settings called the name that members can change its topic, so it read as a second name, as a tester wrote. On Android, iPhone and the desktop the settings now call it the group's name and show the name the group goes by. On the desktop that name is now the group's title, as on the phones: the name a group was created with no longer covers a rename. Rename is offered only where your role may change the name, and a refused rename says so and keeps the name.

releases.title: A deleted message is gone from the replies too
releases.summary: The quote of a reply to a deleted message now says it was deleted, on Android and iPhone, instead of keeping the message's words. On Android, sheets open whole on a tablet in landscape and a theme switch fades once without flashing; on iPhone, a chat's unread count is exact to the second. The iPhone app gets TestFlight build 143013 (1.4.34); the desktop stays at 0.2.70.

changes.title: A reply to a deleted message no longer shows its words
changes.description: A reply carries the words it quotes, so deleting a message left them readable in the quote of every reply to it, in groups and in Saved Messages, as a tester found. Each device now remembers what it deletes, and the quote of a reply to such a message says "Deleted message", keeps the author's name and no longer leads to the message. A reply written on another device is matched by the message's date.

changes.title: Android: sheets from below open whole on a tablet
changes.description: On a tablet in landscape, sheets such as Create group and New contact, and the questions the app asks, opened only a strip at the bottom, as a tester wrote; they now open whole.

changes.title: Android: a theme switch fades once
changes.description: Switching between the light and the dark theme flashed the whole screen a few times; the old theme now fades into the new one once.

changes.title: iPhone: a chat's unread count is exact
changes.description: The unread count of a chat in the list compared message dates with the moment the chat was read to only about two minutes, so a message just read could still count unread, or one that came right after it not; it is now exact to the second.

releases.title: Groups open at once
releases.summary: On Android a group no longer stands still for a moment as it opens, and its name and picture are there with the screen. Only the Android app changes in this release: the iPhone app stays at 1.4.34 (143012) and the desktop at 0.2.70.

changes.title: Android: a group opens at once
changes.description: Opening a group read the list of its members for the side panel before the screen could appear, and read it again at every member event, so in a big group the screen stood still for half a second to a second each time, as a tester wrote, and the group's name and picture filled in after it. The list is now read aside and shown once it is ready, the name and picture come with the screen, and a group opened again shows its member count at once too. With a group of 251 members on a test phone, the screen appeared after 1.1 to 1.7 s before and after 0.14 to 0.27 s now.

releases.title: Calls: every video in its own shape, your picture to drag and swap, on every client
releases.summary: The call screen is redone on Android, iPhone and iPad, and the desktop. Neither video is ever stretched: the other person's fills the screen when it is turned the same way and otherwise shows whole on black. Your own picture keeps your camera's shape, stays clear of the edges, the name and the buttons, goes to the corner you throw it to, and a tap swaps it with the big one. The buttons are even circles with one-line words, and an audio call puts the person in the middle. Also: the attach sheet in the dark theme, a group header when only you are online, and Android 16 screens below the status bar.

changes.title: Video on a call is never stretched
changes.description: The other person's video fills the screen when it is turned the same way as the screen, and shows whole on black when it is not. It is laid out again when either of you turns the phone or the window changes size. On Android, a green strip no longer runs down the edge of the video.

changes.title: Your own picture: your camera's shape, drag it, swap it
changes.description: Your picture in the corner keeps the shape of your camera instead of being squashed into a fixed box. It has rounded corners and stays 16 points clear of the screen's edges, the name and the buttons. Drag it and it goes to the corner you throw it to; tap it and it swaps with the big picture. On Android a long press still makes it bigger, as far as the room between the name and the buttons allows.

changes.title: The call buttons in one even row
changes.description: Equal circles, each with its word on one line: Flip instead of Switch camera, which wrapped to two lines. The camera and the microphone are crossed out while off. On tablets and the desktop the row stays centred.

changes.title: An audio call puts the person in the middle
changes.description: The avatar, the name, the time and the connection stand together in the middle of the screen. The connection, direct or through a relay, is a small dark label under the time on every call. The call screen is dark in the light theme too.

changes.title: Screens stay below the status bar on Android 16
changes.description: Network diagnostics, search, the ringtone and the other screens that went under the clock and the status bar icons on Android 16 now start below them, and their bottoms stay above the gesture bar.

changes.title: A group says when only you are online
changes.description: The header of a group said nobody was online when you were the only one. It now says only you are online.

changes.title: The attach sheet in the dark theme
changes.description: Its top corners show the dimmed chat behind them, not white.

releases.title: Groups: a member to contacts, private messages that stand out, @mentions; the testers' reports on every client
releases.summary: A member of a group can be added to contacts from the group, a message to one member stands out in the feed and only the two of you see it, and @ opens a list of the members, in any script. With the app asleep, a group message now wakes the members who are away. A message deleted in a group stays deleted, your name in a group is kept, and the reports of the testers' group of 21 to 23 November are in on every client. The desktop is signed with a new release key: 0.2.68 and older need one download by hand.

changes.title: A member of a group becomes a contact
changes.description: In a group, “Add to contacts” on a member asks them over the group. When they accept, each of you is in the other's contacts. A member's key copied in a group is recognised in New contact and the search line, which used to say “12 characters missing”: that key is theirs in the group only and is not a Tox ID.

changes.title: Private messages stand out
changes.description: A message written to one member of a group stands on its own ground with a lock and the note “Only you and Name: other members don't see this”. Reply on it answers privately instead of quoting it to the group, and the history of the group never hands it to anyone.

changes.title: @mentions as in Telegram
changes.description: Type @ in a group and pick a member from the list, online members first. Names in Cyrillic, Arabic or any other script work too. A mention is bold, opens the member, and notifies the member mentioned, also in a group that is muted.

changes.title: A group message wakes the phone
changes.description: With the app asleep, a message to a group now wakes the members who are away and are the sender's contacts, with the group, the name and the text, as a contact's message does. When the message then comes over Tox, it does not alert a second time.

changes.title: A deleted group message stays deleted
changes.description: A message deleted in a group no longer comes back when a member who missed the deletion relays the history of the group, also after a restart.

changes.title: A new release key for the desktop
changes.description: Windows, macOS and Linux downloads and the desktop update are signed with a new key, SHA256:LGRvz7I3QsMDWMWGOiVccFADH+RB4h5q7eem1uLHKS0, published in web/downloads. Khandaq 0.2.68 and older trust only the old key, so they do not offer this version: download 0.2.69 once by hand, and it updates itself again from then on.

changes.title: Your name in a group is kept
changes.description: A name set for one group stays after a restart. On the desktop the group's details have “Your name in the group”, and a new profile name reaches every group that has no name of its own.

changes.title: Group messages on iPhone count and notify as a contact's do
changes.description: A message of a member who has left or is offline counts as unread, several messages that come at once notify for the newest, and a group's notification no longer clears the banner of a chat with a person.

changes.title: Sender tiles beside group messages
changes.description: Other members' messages in a group have the sender's tile beside the last message of a run, as in Telegram. A tap on it opens the member.

changes.title: Pause a voice message while recording
changes.description: A recording has Pause and Resume. The message is sent as one, and its length leaves out the time paused.

changes.title: Add more before sending; draw and write on a photo
changes.description: The screen before photos or files go has “+” or “Add more”, which adds to the list instead of starting again. On the phones, Edit offers Crop and rotate or Draw and write; the photo in your library is never changed.

changes.title: Files open in the app
changes.description: A PDF opens in Khandaq, and the viewers have Share. On iPhone audio files play in their message and a video opens in a full player.

changes.title: The keyboard follows a drag
changes.description: Dragging the messages down takes the keyboard down with the finger, and the long-press menu is never under the keyboard.

changes.title: The Windows installer
changes.description: The site offers the installer first. The uninstaller removes the desktop shortcut, the installer carries Khandaq's icon, and tox: links and .tox files open when Khandaq is installed in a folder with spaces.

changes.title: Notes in Saved Messages can be edited
changes.description: Edit on a note changes it in place and marks it edited, whatever its length.

changes.title: Smaller fixes from the testers
changes.description: iPhone: the timer of a hands-free recording no longer stops while you scroll, a swipe on a chat row no longer switches the filter, and a long status wraps. Android: the attach sheet opens whole and Send stays in reach. Desktop: a message you send while scrolled up brings the conversation to its foot.

releases.title: Ideas from the testers on the desktop: read receipts off, files that wait for Send
releases.summary: The desktop part of the first batch of ideas from the testers' group; the phones got theirs in 0.2.67. Read receipts can be turned off. Files you pick, paste or drop wait for Send. A chat opens at the first message you have not read, under the line “Unread messages”. A chat with words typed and not sent shows them as a draft in the list, a new profile can take a photo on its first screen, and on a Mac tox: links and .tox profile files reach the app.

changes.title: Read receipts can be turned off
changes.description: Settings › Privacy has “Send read receipts” under “Show that I'm typing”. It is on until you turn it off. With it off, your contacts don't see that you have read their messages; you still see that they have read yours.

changes.title: Files wait for Send
changes.description: Files you pick with the paperclip, paste or drop are listed first, with a thumbnail for photos, the name and the size. Enter sends them, Esc or Cancel keeps them back, in chats and in groups. A web address dropped on a conversation goes into the field instead of being sent.

changes.title: Chats open at “Unread messages”
changes.description: A chat or a group that got messages while it was not in front opens at the first of them, under the line “Unread messages”. The line stays while the conversation is open.

changes.title: A photo for a new profile
changes.description: The first screen of a new profile, where you choose your name, has an optional photo tile, with the same picker as You › photo.

changes.title: tox: links on macOS
changes.description: A tox: link or a .tox profile file opened on a Mac now reaches the app, also the one it is started with.

changes.title: Drafts in the list
changes.description: A chat with words typed and not sent shows “Draft:” and the words in the list, until you send them, clear the field or close the app.

changes.title: The day strip says its hours are hours online
changes.description: The hint beside a contact's day strip now says what its hours are: “online in the past day: 7:00 to 9:00”, “usually online 19:00 to 22:00”.

releases.title: Ideas from the testers: privacy switches, files that wait for Send, unread messages first
releases.summary: The first batch of ideas from the testers' group, on Android and iPhone. Read receipts and typing can be turned off. A photo from the camera, a document or a file waits for Send instead of going at once. A chat or a group opens at the first message you have not read, under the line “Unread messages”. Voice messages play at 1.5x and 2x, Android gets a reaction bar, tox: links open New contact, and a new profile can take a photo on its first screen. The desktop gets its part of the batch in 0.2.68.

changes.title: Read receipts and typing can be turned off
changes.description: Settings › Privacy has “Send read receipts” and “Show that I'm typing”. Both are on until you turn them off. With read receipts off, your contacts don't see that you have read their messages; you still see that they have read yours. With typing off, nobody sees that you are typing.

changes.title: Nothing is sent by accident
changes.description: A photo from the camera, a document or a file now waits for Send. Android shows a camera shot in the preview and asks before a document goes. iPhone asks with a sheet that names the file and its size, and the photo preview has one Send button instead of two. Cancel, Back and a swipe send nothing.

changes.title: Chats open at “Unread messages”
changes.description: A chat or a group that got messages while it was closed opens at the first of them, under the line “Unread messages”. iPhone did this in chats with one person and now does it in groups too.

changes.title: Voice messages at 1.5x and 2x
changes.description: The voice message that plays has a pill that switches between 1x, 1.5x and 2x. The app keeps your choice for the next ones.

changes.title: Android: reactions in one tap
changes.description: Hold a message and a bar of reactions appears over it; one tap reacts, as on iPhone.

changes.title: tox: links open New contact
changes.description: A tox: link opened from a browser, another app or a QR code opens New contact with the ID filled in and checked; the request goes only when you send it. A link opened before you sign in waits until you are in. On Android a link with a group key opens Join group.

changes.title: A photo for a new profile
changes.description: The first screen of a new profile, where you choose your name, has a place for a photo. It is optional and uses the same picker and crop as You.

changes.title: iPhone: Language in Settings, and edits in groups
changes.description: Language is now the second row of Settings. The app carries only the four languages it speaks, English, Russian, Arabic and Chinese, so the system no longer shows its own texts in German or French. Your own messages in a group can be edited from the menu, as in a chat with one person. An edit longer than one message can carry (1300 bytes, about 650 Cyrillic letters) used to change the text on your phone only; now the editor asks you to shorten it or to send it as a new message.

changes.title: Android: your language in calls and notifications
changes.description: The call notification and its buttons, the crash screen and the lines a group writes (created, who can join, roles) are now in Russian, Arabic and Chinese too, and a group line names the group instead of “#G1”. Settings › Notifications has “Background notification”: it opens the phone's settings, where that notification can be hidden while messages still arrive.

changes.title: The day strip says its hours are hours online
changes.description: The hint beside a contact's day strip now says what its hours are: “online in the past day: 7:00 to 9:00”, “usually online 19:00 to 22:00”. On Android the line under your name, which says whether you are online, sits right under it again.

releases.title: The desktop updates itself
releases.summary: The desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux now finds a new version by itself, and on Windows and macOS puts it in place when you press Update. It checks khandaq.org a few minutes after it starts and then once a day, and believes only a description of the release signed with the Khandaq release key built into the app. Nothing is downloaded until you ask. Settings › About has the switch.

changes.title: Desktop: the app updates itself
changes.description: A few minutes after it starts, and then once a day, the desktop app asks khandaq.org whether a newer version is out. When one is, a band says so and links to what is new. Press Update and the app downloads that version, checks it and puts it in place. On Windows the installer runs by itself and starts Khandaq again; a portable copy swaps its folder and keeps your profiles and settings, and if anything goes wrong it puts the old copy back without removing anything of yours. On macOS the new app takes the place of the old one and starts. On Linux the band leads to the download, which you install as before. The app believes only a description signed with the Khandaq release key built into it, the download must have the size and SHA-256 that description gives, and it never offers an older version. This is the first version with the check: from 0.2.64 or older, download this one by hand.

changes.title: Desktop: the check is yours to turn off
changes.description: Settings › About has the switch “Check for updates” and the button “Check now”, which checks at once even with the switch off. A check is two small downloads from khandaq.org, through your profile's proxy if one is set, with no cookies and no version number in them; khandaq.org sees the address it comes from, as with any visit to the site, and nothing about your contacts or messages. Test builds do not check.

releases.title: Old group messages arrive quietly; the All folder shows; a flick leaves the chat
releases.summary: When a group catches up on the messages you missed, Android no longer notifies of each of them: a message from the group's history notifies only if it was sent in the last 45 seconds. The chat list shows All as its first folder, on iPhone and Android, so the sideways swipe goes between folders you can see. On iPhone a quick flick to the right across the messages leaves a chat or a group, the menu of a pinned message offers Unpin, and holding a chat in the list offers Delete.

changes.title: Android: no notifications for old group messages
changes.description: When a group caught up on the messages its members had exchanged while you were away, Android notified of every one of them, however old: a tester got notifications for messages from hours before. A message that comes from the group's history now goes into the chat without a notification when it was sent more than 45 seconds ago; one sent just now still notifies, as a message that arrives live does. iPhone and the desktop never notified of history.

changes.title: The All folder is visible
changes.description: The chat list had a folder for all chats with no button of its own: the sideways swipe and a second tap on a folder led to it, and it looked as if the folders changed by themselves. All now stands first among the folders, on iPhone and Android, and the swipe goes from one to the next.

changes.title: iPhone: a flick leaves the chat
changes.description: Besides the swipe from the edge of the screen, a quick flick to the right anywhere on the messages now leaves a chat or a group, as in Telegram; in a right-to-left language it is a flick to the left. A slow short drag leaves the chat where it is, and a swipe the other way still answers a message.

changes.title: iPhone: Unpin in the menu of a pinned message
changes.description: Holding a pinned message offered Pin again. It now offers Unpin, in a chat and in a group, as the cross on the pinned strip does.

changes.title: iPhone: Delete in the menu of a chat
changes.description: Holding a chat in the list now offers Delete, with the same confirmation as before: the sideways swipe on the list goes between folders, so it does not delete.

releases.title: A reaction wakes the phone; the notification says what came
releases.summary: A reaction to your message now wakes your phone the way a new message does, in a chat with a person and in a group. The notification of either says what came: the text, a voice message, a video, a photo, a file, or which reaction to which message. It is sealed on the sender's phone with a key only your phone can work out, so the push relay, Google and Apple carry it unread. The desktop tells you when someone reacts to your message.

changes.title: A reaction wakes the phone
changes.description: A reaction to your message did not wake your phone: you saw it only the next time the app was open. Now a reaction to a contact's message wakes their phone when they are offline, as a new message does: in a chat with a person, and in a group when the author of the message is one of your contacts. It works once both phones have this update. Taking a reaction back never wakes anyone.

changes.title: The notification says what came
changes.description: A push said only "New message". It now shows the text, or that a voice message, a video, a photo or a file came, or which reaction was set to which of your messages, in chats with a person and in groups. The preview is sealed on the sender's phone with a key that only the receiving phone can work out, and only a contact you still have can send one; the push relay, Google and Apple carry it unread. With message text turned off in the settings, a notification says only who it is from and "New message" or "New reaction". A voice message is one recorded in the app; another sound file is a file with its name.

changes.title: Android: two wakeups close together no longer close the app
changes.description: When the phone was woken twice within 20 seconds, by two pushes or by a push and the app's own timer, the app closed in the background 20 seconds after the second. With a push for every message and reaction since this release, that would have been common. Each wakeup now keeps the phone awake and lets it sleep again on its own.

changes.title: Desktop: notifications of reactions
changes.description: When someone reacts to your message, in a chat with a person or in a group, the desktop says who it was, which reaction and to what: "Reacted 👍 to “See you at six”", or to your voice message, video, photo or file. A muted chat stays quiet, and in a group that notifies only of mentions, a reaction to your message counts as one. With message text hidden in the notification settings, it says only that a reaction came. A notification of a file names a voice message, a video or a photo as such, with its size, and any other file by its name.

changes.title: Push relay: sealed previews
changes.description: The relay passes a sealed preview on as it came: to Android as data, to iPhone as an alert the phone opens before it shows it. Each event gives one alert, a repeat of it stays silent, and past the per-device limit a wake goes out plain. Older apps and their wakes are unchanged. A failed send is written to the log as one line.

releases.title: React from the desktop; groups keep relays of their own
releases.summary: The desktop can react to a message, as the phones do, and when it comes back online it gets the messages a public group posted while it was away. Every group now keeps relays of its own, so members behind one router, or on a network that blocks UDP, can still reach each other. A message passed on from a group's history shows once, under its author's name. On iPhone a file shows that it is opening, and a reaction on a group file now reaches Android and the desktop.

changes.title: Groups keep relays of their own
changes.description: Two members behind one router, or on a network that blocks UDP, could stay apart in a group while both were online: a group used only the relays the app was already connected to, and often had none, above all in a group made or opened before the app was connected. Each group now keeps up to three relays of its own, and an invitation brings them to the new member, so members who cannot reach each other directly meet through a relay. It works best once everyone in the group has this update.

changes.title: Desktop: react to a message
changes.description: The message menu has React, with the seven emoji of the phones, in chats with a person and in groups, on texts and on files. The same emoji again takes your reaction back, another one replaces it. A person who is offline gets it when they connect.

changes.title: Desktop: group messages posted while you were away
changes.description: A message posted in a public group while the desktop was offline never reached it. When the desktop comes back, members who have the message pass it on, and it shows with the time it was written, without a notification. Until the group knows its author, the message is signed with the start of their key, then with their name.

changes.title: Group history comes once, under its author's name
changes.description: A message that members pass on from a group's history could show a second time on iPhone, signed with the end of a key instead of a name, when it had already come live. iPhone now knows every passed-on copy of a message it has, Android passes a message on under the name its author had, and iPhone passes on the message of a member who left under that member's own key and name, not under those of whoever joined after.

changes.title: Reactions on group files reach everyone
changes.description: A reaction set on iPhone to a photo or file in a group did not show on Android or on the desktop. iPhone now says who reacted, and Android and the desktop accept such a reaction from an older iPhone too.

changes.title: iPhone: the name and the role over a message in a group
changes.description: A member's message could show "founder" or another role that was not theirs, once someone else had come back to the group in their old place, and a chat opened before the group connected showed no role at all. The role next to a name is now always that member's own and shows as soon as the group knows its members. A member's name is also one colour on all their messages, the ones passed on from the group's history too.

changes.title: iPhone: the messages you pick in a group stay picked
changes.description: In a group, the messages you picked to delete or copy could come unpicked when a member came or left or the group's history arrived, and Delete then did nothing. They now stay picked.

changes.title: iPhone: a file shows that it is opening
changes.description: A PDF or another file took a few seconds to open with nothing on the screen. A spinner now shows until it opens, and its Cancel button is in the language of the app.

releases.title: Screen readers say what a reply answers
releases.summary: VoiceOver on iPhone and TalkBack on Android now say which message a reply answers before they read it, as the desktop does. On Android a group message that reached you after you came back online shows the time it was written. On iPhone a quote keeps the space where the quoted message had a line break.

changes.title: Screen readers: a reply says what it answers
changes.description: VoiceOver and TalkBack read a reply as if it were a message of its own. Now they say "In reply to", the name and the quoted words, then the reply.

changes.title: Android: missed group messages show when they were written
changes.description: A group message that reached you after you came back online showed the time it arrived, not the time it was written, among messages sorted by the time they were written. It shows when it was written now.

changes.title: iPhone: a quote keeps the space between lines
changes.description: When the quoted message had a line break, the last word of one line and the first word of the next ran together in the quote, on the iPhone and in the quote it sent to others. They stay apart now.

changes.title: iPhone: VoiceOver names the connection once
changes.description: At the top of a chat VoiceOver said the kind of connection twice, for example "direct link. direct link.". It says it once now.

releases.title: Files of any size open on iPhone; reactions look the same everywhere
releases.summary: On iPhone a big video or photo now shows in the chat like a small one, with its picture and, for a video, its length, and a file shown as a row opens with a tap. The desktop and iPhone show reactions as chips with the emoji and the count, as Android does, so a reaction set on a phone looks the same on the desktop.

changes.title: iPhone: big videos and photos show in the chat
changes.description: A video or photo over 20 MB came to an iPhone as a plain file row, and a tap on the row opened nothing. Now a video of any size shows its first frame and its length, a photo shows itself, and a tap opens them. A file that stays a row, such as a PDF, opens with a tap anywhere on the row once it has arrived. A big video you send shows the same way.

changes.title: Reactions look the same everywhere
changes.description: A reaction set on a phone, especially one from the full emoji keyboard, showed on the desktop as a small grey symbol under the message. The desktop and iPhone now show each reaction as a chip with the emoji and how many people chose it, as Android does. On iPhone your own reaction is highlighted.

changes.title: iPhone: a video keeps its length
changes.description: The length in the corner of a video disappeared when its message was drawn again, for example after a reaction or a new message. It stays now.

releases.title: Invitations wait for an offline contact; voice messages from the desktop
releases.summary: A contact who is offline can now be invited to a group: the invitation waits on your device and goes once they are online. The desktop apps send voice messages and emoji, paste pictures and files, and can make the whole interface larger. The author's name stands apart from the message, Khandaq Community keeps its sound and shows the Khandaq logo, and on Android the send button is visible again. Big group files keep going when a member's network changes or the sender's app restarts.

changes.title: Invite a contact who is offline
changes.description: A group invitation goes only while both of you are online, so a contact who was offline could not be invited. Khandaq now keeps the invitation on your device for up to 30 days and sends it as soon as the contact is online. New group and the contact's menu offer offline contacts, and the notice after inviting says how many invitations went and how many wait.

changes.title: Desktop: voice messages and emoji
changes.description: The desktop apps could not send a voice message or an emoji. The microphone button next to the field records a voice message of up to five minutes, which the phones play like their own, and the list shows it as a voice message. The emoji button opens the emoji set.

changes.title: Desktop: interface size
changes.description: Settings > Appearance > Interface size makes the whole window larger, from 100% to 200%, for screens where everything looked small. Khandaq offers to restart and comes back at the new size. A size the screen has no room for is not offered.

changes.title: Paste pictures and files
changes.description: On the desktop, Ctrl+V pastes a picture into a group as it did in a chat, and a file copied in Finder or a Linux file manager is sent as the file instead of its name. On iPhone and Android, a pasted photo opens the send preview.

changes.title: Big group files keep going
changes.description: A member whose network address changes, for example from Wi-Fi to mobile data, is reached again at once instead of after about a minute, so a big file sent to them goes on. When the desktop or iPhone app that sent the file is restarted, it still sends a member the parts they are missing.

changes.title: Who wrote it
changes.description: In chats and groups, the author's name now stands apart from the text under it, and You over your own messages takes the same colour as other names instead of reading as a line of the message.

changes.title: Khandaq Community keeps its sound
changes.description: Khandaq Community is no longer muted when you join it, and if an earlier version muted it, it is heard again once after this update. Its picture is the Khandaq logo.

changes.title: Android: the send button
changes.description: On Android 16 in the light theme, the send button was a black square with the arrow hardly visible. The arrow is back, and the bar that appears when you select messages matches the app.

changes.title: Rename a contact
changes.description: On the desktop, a contact is renamed in place in the chat header, with the whole name in view. On iPhone and Android, Rename is in the menu of a contact in the list.

changes.title: Desktop: profile and group header
changes.description: Copy ID sits right under your ID in the profile, where you look for it. The group header no longer says that groups have no calls.

releases.title: Big group files reach a member who lost the network
releases.summary: A big file sent to a group now reaches a member whose network dropped for a few seconds while it came, on every platform. On Android, a group you leave or delete with nobody else online no longer comes back when Khandaq is closed right after. On the desktop, a friend's invite brings you into a group you joined by its ID. Over a reply to your own message, the bar now says In reply to yourself.

changes.title: Big files in groups reach everyone
changes.description: A big file sent to a group stopped for a member who lost the network for a few seconds while it came, and the sender gave it up about a minute later. The Tox core library that all Khandaq apps share now keeps what arrives out of order, confirms what it got, and starts clean with a member who connects again. On Android, a file is no longer taken as downloaded while parts of it are missing, and it goes on when its sender is back. A member whose network address changes, for example from Wi-Fi to mobile data, is reached again after about a minute, and the file goes on from there.

changes.title: Android: a group you leave stays left
changes.description: A group you left or deleted while no other member was online could come back if Khandaq was closed right after. It now stays gone.

changes.title: Desktop: joining a group by its ID
changes.description: After you joined a group by its ID, an invite from a friend inside it did not bring you in, and you stayed out of the group. The invite now completes the join.

changes.title: In reply to yourself
changes.description: Over a reply to your own message, the bar above the field said In reply to You, which read wrong in Russian. It now says In reply to yourself.

releases.title: Reply on the desktop, and the author's name opens the member
releases.summary: On Windows, macOS and Linux you can now reply to a message or a file from its menu, and the reply reaches phones with its quote. In a group, the name over a message opens that member: write privately, mute and more. On Android, a reply to your own message shows the others your name instead of You.

changes.title: Reply on the desktop
changes.description: Right-click a message or a file and choose Reply, the first item of the menu. The bar above the field shows whom you answer and the start of their words, and the cross cancels it. The reply reaches Android and iPhone as a reply with its quote, and their replies show on the desktop as before. A reply to your own message carries your name to the others.

changes.title: The author's name opens the member
changes.description: In a group, click or tap the name over someone's message to open the same menu as their row in the member list: write privately, copy key, mute, and on phones add to contacts. Before, the name did nothing.

changes.title: Android: your name in replies to your own message
changes.description: A reply to your own message showed the others the word You in its quote. It now shows your name, as iPhone does since 0.2.56.

changes.title: Right clicks no longer select text
changes.description: On the desktop, every third right click in a row selected the text of a message. Now only left clicks select.

releases.title: Two teal checks when a message is seen, files that go on after the network drops, and Khandaq Community
releases.summary: In a chat with one person, the second check turns teal once they have seen your message. A file between two people goes on from where it stopped when the network changes or drops for a moment, and files from your contacts download by themselves up to 200 MB. Every Khandaq app joins Khandaq Community, the shared group of Khandaq users, once and muted; you can leave it. Group files ask for the parts they miss, groups are found by their ID, and group files reach phones on IPv6 networks. The fixes are in Khandaq for the computer 0.2.57, Android 0.2.57 and iPhone build 143001.

changes.title: Two teal checks once your message is seen
changes.description: In a chat with one person, the second check now turns teal once they have opened the chat and seen your message or file. Grey checks still mean sent and delivered. Groups keep their marks as before. A contact on 0.2.56 or older sends no read receipts, so their checks stay grey.

changes.title: A file goes on after the network drops
changes.description: A file between two people that stopped because the network changed, or because one of you was offline for a moment, now goes on from where it stopped once you are both back. Before, it failed or started again from the beginning. On iPhone it waits with its bar instead of saying Not sent.

changes.title: Files from your contacts download by themselves
changes.description: Files and photos from your contacts now download as they come, up to 200 MB each, so they are there when you open the chat. Bigger files still wait for a tap.

changes.title: Khandaq Community
changes.description: Every Khandaq app joins Khandaq Community, the shared group of Khandaq users, once by itself. It is muted, stays at the top of your chats and is always called Khandaq Community. You can leave it like any other group, and it does not join again by itself. Files that others post there wait for your tap.

changes.title: Group files ask for the parts they miss
changes.description: A member who missed parts of a group file now asks the sender for just those parts and gets them, between every pair of Khandaq apps. Members reached through a relay get the file at a pace the relay can carry, instead of losing most of it.

changes.title: Groups are found by their ID
changes.description: A group joined by its ID is now looked up on the network by that ID, so it is found even when its only member online is the founder. Before, members looked for each other in different places and often met only through an invitation.

changes.title: Group files reach phones on IPv6 networks
changes.description: On a direct IPv6 path, every full part of a group file was a few bytes too big and was lost on the way, so the file never arrived while the group looked connected. Group packets now fit every IPv6 path. A member still on 0.2.56 sends the old size, so they need the update too.

changes.title: iPhone: group settings no longer close the app
changes.description: Opening the settings of a public group closed Khandaq on iPhone. Photos and files of groups also stay when the app starts again, and a group you joined by invitation is still there after a restart.

changes.title: The Mac app stays online in the background
changes.description: macOS put Khandaq to sleep (App Nap) while its window was hidden, so it went offline after a while. It now stays online.

changes.title: A calm No network band
changes.description: When the device has had no network for 3 seconds, a band at the top says No network, then Connecting and Back online.

changes.title: Report a message in a group
changes.description: A message someone else wrote in a group can be reported: Report opens a mail to Khandaq support with the message, its author and the time it was written.

changes.title: A file you declined comes again only by your tap
changes.description: A file you declined or cancelled is no longer downloaded again by itself when it is offered again. Before, a refused file could be sent again in full in the background.

changes.title: A file warning no longer locks the window
changes.description: On the computer, a folder Khandaq could not save to showed its warning inside the file card, cut off and catching every click. The warning now covers the window, OK asks for another folder, and the save question opens in Downloads when the saved folder is gone.

changes.title: Quieter lists
changes.description: On Android, your photo no longer blinks in the chat list when a contact comes online, and the scrollbar shows only while you scroll. On iPhone, a muted group adds nothing to the badges, and a file name in Cyrillic, Arabic or Chinese stays as it was.

releases.title: Long texts go whole, groups hold what nobody can get yet, and a reply is a swipe
releases.summary: On iPhone, a file that comes in a group no longer closes the app. A text of any length now goes whole, as several messages in order. A message or a file written while nobody else is in a group waits and goes when someone comes, instead of showing as sent and reaching nobody. New groups are open to anyone with the group key. A message is answered by swiping it to the left, as in Telegram, and a voice note plays from a round Play button. Big files show a bar while they are prepared, and Android wakes your contacts' phones by default. The fixes are in Khandaq for the computer 0.2.56, Android 0.2.56 and iPhone build 142999.

changes.title: iPhone no longer closes when a file comes in a group
changes.description: Any file another member sent to a group, a small photo as much as a video, closed Khandaq on iPhone as it arrived: the app read its database from the wrong thread. The file now comes in as it should.

changes.title: A long text goes whole, as several messages
changes.description: A text longer than one message was refused, cut at the limit or, on iPhone, stopped at 1000 characters while you typed or pasted it. It now goes as several messages, cut at a line break or a space, in order, and the counter under the field says how many. There is no upper limit. Texts in groups, captions, shared texts and forwards go the same way.

changes.title: A message written while nobody else is in the group waits for someone
changes.description: A group sends a message only to the members it has already reached. Right after a group was made or opened, and while everybody else was away, a message was shown as sent and reached nobody. Such a message now waits with the in-transit mark and goes, in the order written, once another member is there; it also waits through a restart of the app. A file sent to such a group waits too: on the phones until someone comes, on the computer for two minutes, then it says Not sent.

changes.title: New groups are open to anyone with the group key
changes.description: A new group was by invitation only, yet its card still offered the group key, and joining with that key waited forever. A new group is now open to anyone with its key; By invitation only is one tap away, and such a group shows no key or QR code. The founder can change this later. Groups you already have keep their setting. On Android, a group joined by its key now connects: the app read the group's connection state wrongly.

changes.title: Back works on Android 16
changes.description: On Android 16 the Back button and the swipe from the edge closed Settings, the profile, the member list and even the call screen in one step. Back now steps back one screen at a time again: an open panel or a search closes first.

changes.title: Android wakes your contacts' phones by default
changes.description: Wake-ups let a sleeping phone know that a message or a call is waiting. They were off on Android since version 0.2.7 and could not be turned on, so no Android phone published the address it can be woken at. They are on now, also after the update. A long text wakes a contact once, not once per part. On iPhone, a wake-up now reconnects at once instead of only waiting.

changes.title: The first contact of a profile that starts with a group gets its messages
changes.description: On Android, a profile that had a group but no contact yet lost track of its first contact until the next start: that contact's messages and files did not show in the chat, and files to them did not go.

changes.title: Swipe a message to the left to reply
changes.description: A message is answered by swiping it to the left, as in Telegram (to the right in Arabic). A reply badge grows as the message slides, and a light tick says when letting go will reply.

changes.title: A voice note plays from a round Play button
changes.description: The word Listen gave way to a round Play button, as in Telegram; it turns into Pause while the note plays. Screen readers still say Listen and Pause.

changes.title: Big files show a bar while they are prepared
changes.description: A big file from the gallery showed nothing until it had been copied for sending. It now appears in the chat at once, with Preparing the file, a bar and Cancel. On iPhone, the video banner no longer disappears by itself, and picked media keep their order. On the computer, a big file goes into a group at a pace, with a bar, and the window no longer freezes while it goes.

changes.title: A group file that goes on downloading after a restart comes out whole
changes.description: On Android, a group file whose download went on after the app restarted came out with zeros in place of everything that had arrived before the restart, and was offered as finished. A resumed download now keeps what it has. A download left half-done by an earlier version starts again from the beginning.

changes.title: Groups on the computer: a group key in the search, a group that stays
changes.description: A group key pasted into the search offers the group, or opens it if you are already in it. A group joined by its ID no longer disappears when the app is closed before the group has synced, and an invitation that cannot be accepted is said, instead of leaving an empty row.

changes.title: Group messages arrive once and in order
changes.description: On iPhone, the first member to join a group got the messages its founder had written alone twice, and the parts of a long text from Android could show in the wrong order. Each message now comes once, and parts keep their order. Android stamps the parts of a long text a second apart, so older iPhones show them in order too.

changes.title: Files in groups on the computer: received stays received, authors in full
changes.description: After a restart, every file a member had sent to a group showed as one of yours that did not go. It now stays received, with Open and Show in folder. Over each run of messages in a group the author's whole name is shown, as on the phones, instead of only the first word. The member count says online only for members a message can actually reach.

changes.title: A reply to your own message carries your name
changes.description: Replying to your own message showed the others the word You as the author of the quote. It now shows your name, as they know you.

changes.title: Paste takes the text, not a picture of it
changes.description: A text copied from Excel or Word was pasted as a picture. The text now wins over a picture that comes with it, and typing after a very long paste no longer slows down.

releases.title: Leaving a group reaches the others even through a relay
releases.summary: A member who leaves a group sends the others a short notice first. Through a relay that notice could be lost, and the others then kept the member listed for about a minute. Khandaq now keeps a group you leave in the background for 12 seconds, so the notice can be sent again; for you the group is gone at once. The fix is in Khandaq for the computer 0.2.55, Android 0.2.55 and iPhone build 142998.

changes.title: Your leave reaches the group even through a relay
changes.description: Leaving a group sends the other members a short notice, and right after it the app let go of the group, so the notice had a single try. Through a relay it was sometimes lost, and the others kept you listed, as online, for about a minute. The app now keeps the group in the background for 12 seconds after you leave, long enough for the notice to be sent again; for you the group is gone at once. If the app is closed or stops in those seconds, it finishes leaving when it next starts. Joining the group again in those seconds works as any join.

changes.title: A late invitation does not bring you back into a group you left
changes.description: Joining a group by its ID also asks your friends who are in it to invite you. An invitation that came after you had left the group took you back in at once. It now waits as a card with Join, like any invitation.

releases.title: Android: leaving a group shows at once, and your ID stays the same
releases.summary: Khandaq for Android 0.2.54 fixes what our live checks across phones and computers turned up. A member who leaves a group is taken off the list at once, and closing the app is not taken for leaving. Adding a contact no longer changes your ID behind your back. A long message goes as several messages instead of being cut, a file you send keeps its name, and joined emoji such as the heart on fire are drawn whole.

changes.title: A member who leaves a group is gone at once
changes.description: Leaving a group now sends the other members a short notice first. Android takes the member off the member list, the counts and the group page as soon as the notice arrives, and writes that they left once. Before, a member who had left could stay listed. If the notice is lost on the way, as can happen through a relay, the member goes when the exit itself comes through. Closing the app is not leaving: a member who only closed it stays in the group, offline.

changes.title: Your ID no longer changes when you add a contact
changes.description: Each contact you added, or whose request you accepted, gave your ID a new antispam part without a word, so the ID you had shared stopped working and requests sent to it were lost. The antispam part now changes only when you ask for it, under You, Change antispam. An ID that has already changed is not brought back: if you added contacts after sharing your ID, share your current ID again.

changes.title: A long message goes as several messages instead of being cut
changes.description: A direct message longer than one message can carry lost its end. It now goes as several messages, cut between whole characters, whether the contact is online or the message waits for them.

changes.title: A file you send keeps its name
changes.description: A photo or a file sent from Android reached the other side under a made-up name such as 9ded_1000000022.png. It now goes out under the name it was picked with; for a photo picked from the phone's own gallery the gallery's name is used.

changes.title: File entries keep their layout and Save to phone
changes.description: After several files in a row, an entry could show a squeezed name with a blank gap under it, or have no Save to phone at all, even after the chat was reopened. Each entry now keeps its own layout and its Save to phone.

changes.title: A contact whose request you accepted is not waiting for your reply
changes.description: Right after you accepted someone's contact request, Android showed them as your own unanswered request until they first came online. They now read like any other offline contact.

changes.title: Chat previews keep whole characters and drop byte counts
changes.description: A preview in the chat list, in a notification or of a draft could end in half an emoji, and the preview of a file showed its size in bytes. A preview is now cut between whole characters, and a file's preview shows its name.

changes.title: The group page shows a join or a leave at once
changes.description: The group page showed the old member count for up to three seconds after someone joined or left, and could drop a member who had only closed the app until the list was read again. An offline founder was shown as a plain member. The count now changes at once, a member who closed the app stays, and the founder stays the founder.

changes.title: Joined emoji such as ❤️‍🔥 are whole
changes.description: Joined emoji that the app's emoji set has no picture of, such as the heart on fire, were drawn in pieces in messages and in the message field. When the phone's own font has the emoji, it now draws it whole. A few joined emoji that the emoji picker does not offer stay drawn apart.

releases.title: Leaving a group shows at once, and emoji are whole on the computer
releases.summary: A member who leaves a group now tells the others, and Khandaq for the computer and for iPhone take them off the list at once instead of about a minute later. Closing the app is no longer taken for leaving. On the computer, emoji with a skin tone and joined emoji are drawn whole and as big as the others, and Listen plays a voice message without asking where to save it. iPhone build 142997 carries the iPhone side of these fixes.

changes.title: A member who leaves a group is gone at once
changes.description: Leaving a group now sends the other members a short notice first. Khandaq for the computer and for iPhone take the member off the list and the count as soon as the notice arrives; before, the member stayed listed, as online, for about a minute. If the notice is lost on the way, as can happen through a relay, the member goes after that minute, as before. Closing the app is not leaving: a member who only closed it stays in the group, offline, and is not shown as having left.

changes.title: Emoji with a skin tone and joined emoji are whole on the computer
changes.description: The computer drew 👍🏽 as a thumb and a coloured square, 🏴‍☠️ as a flag and a skull, and 👨‍⚕️ as a man and a staff, in messages, in the message field and in the row of a message on its way. Each is now one emoji, set in the system's colour emoji font and as big as the emoji around it. On the Mac and Linux so are flags and keycaps such as 🇹🇷 and 1️⃣. Windows has no colour flags, so there flags and keycaps stay in the font of the text around them, as before. A few joined emoji that the phones' emoji picker does not offer stay drawn apart, as on Android.

changes.title: Listen plays a voice message without asking where to save it
changes.description: A voice message that waited for Accept had to be saved somewhere through a file dialog before Listen would play it. Listen now fetches it into the app's own folder and plays it when it is here; Accept fetches it the same way without playing. Nothing comes unless you press one of them.

changes.title: No stray “_” after each message to an iPhone
changes.description: Every message the computer sent to an iPhone came back as a new message from the iPhone that read only “_”. The iPhone sent a delivery receipt for a message that had nothing to confirm; it no longer does, and the computer ignores such receipts.

changes.title: Group messages that reach the computer count as delivered
changes.description: The phones confirm every group message they show to its author, and the computer did not. A phone's message in a group of computers stayed at sent, and the phone kept asking the group for it again. The computer now confirms the messages it shows.

changes.title: A contact whose request you accepted is not waiting for your reply
changes.description: Right after you accepted someone's contact request, the computer and iPhone showed them as your own unanswered request until they first came online. They now read like any other offline contact. A contact you asked yourself still reads as waiting for a reply.

changes.title: A caption sent with a photo stays with the photo on iPhone
changes.description: On the iPhone that sent a photo with a caption, the caption often showed as a separate message above the photo. It now joins the photo's bubble.

changes.title: A group's online count on iPhone leaves you out
changes.description: The chat list on iPhone counted you among a group's members online, one more than the group's header. It now counts only the others, like the computer and Android.

changes.title: The paperclip menu on iPhone works with VoiceOver
changes.description: Gallery, Camera, Audio, File and Location are read by name, VoiceOver stays inside the menu, and the escape gesture closes it. The rows of the message menu, the two cards of an empty contact list and the caption field before sending are read by name too.

changes.title: Leave group in the computer's chat list speaks of the group
changes.description: It opened the question for a contact, “Remove friend”. It now asks to leave the group, in the words of the group's page.

releases.title: Mac notifications next to the iPhone app, and FFmpeg 8.1.3
releases.summary: On a Mac that also has Khandaq for iPhone installed, macOS refused the Mac app's message notifications, because both apps carried the same identifier. The Mac app now has its own. The Windows, Mac and Linux apps carry FFmpeg 8.1.3, the newest release of the 8.1 line.

changes.title: New-message notifications show on a Mac that also has Khandaq for iPhone
changes.description: Macs with Apple silicon can install the iPhone app, and it shares the identifier org.khandaq.messenger with the Mac app. On such a Mac, macOS took the Mac app for the iPhone app and refused its notifications without a word. The Mac app is now org.khandaq.desktop. Your profiles, settings and history stay where they are, but macOS meets the app as a new one once: it asks again before showing notifications, before the first call uses the microphone or the camera, and before you share your screen. If you let the app open your profile without asking for its password, macOS also asks once whether Khandaq may use the password it keeps in the keychain: enter your Mac password and choose Always Allow. If Khandaq for iPhone is in your Applications folder, it holds the name Khandaq there, so keep the Mac app in another folder, for example the Applications folder in your home folder, and do not let Finder replace one with the other.

changes.title: FFmpeg 8.1.3 in the Windows, Mac and Linux apps
changes.description: The three desktop apps read voice messages, the camera and video calls with FFmpeg 8.1.3, the newest release of the 8.1 line, built as before with only the parts the app uses. NVD lists 16 advisories against 8.1.3, down from 35 against 8.1.1. The MP4 reader still skips the kinds of boxes with known bugs and no fixed FFmpeg 8.1 release yet (CVE-2026-52297, CVE-2026-96611, CVE-2026-107678).

releases.title: Voice messages play in the Windows app
releases.summary: The Windows app plays voice messages from the phones in the chat, as the Mac and Linux apps do, instead of opening them in the system's player. It now carries FFmpeg 8.1.1 built for it, like the Mac and Linux apps, in place of FFmpeg 4.4.8.

changes.title: Voice messages from the phones play in the Windows app
The Windows app carries FFmpeg 8.1.1 built for it, like the Mac and Linux apps

releases.title: Files from contacts wait for you to accept them
releases.summary: A new installation no longer saves the files a contact sends you by itself: each one waits in the chat until you accept it. The Linux app reads voice messages with an FFmpeg built for it, which skips the parts of MP4 files with known bugs, instead of Ubuntu's FFmpeg 6.1.1.

changes.title: Files from a contact wait for Accept on a new installation
changes.description: Until now a new installation saved every file a contact sent you into the downloads folder by itself, before you had looked at it. Now it starts with Settings > Network > Download attachments set to Never: each file waits in the chat until you press Accept. Always and Small files are still there to choose, and an installation that already has a choice keeps it. A folder you set for a contact still takes their files, and files sent in a group are saved as before.

changes.title: Voice messages on Linux are read with a hardened FFmpeg
changes.description: The Linux app used Ubuntu's FFmpeg 6.1.1 with every format Ubuntu builds in, and Ubuntu has not yet fixed CVE-2026-107678 in it: a crafted MP4 file can make FFmpeg exhaust its stack, and a voice message is an MP4 file the app reads when you press play. The Linux app now carries FFmpeg 8.1.1 with only the parts it uses for the camera, voice messages and video calls, with no network access and no filters. As in the Mac app, its MP4 reader skips the kinds of boxes that have known bugs and no fixed FFmpeg 8.1 release yet (CVE-2026-52297, CVE-2026-96611, CVE-2026-107678). The libraries that came only with Ubuntu's FFmpeg are gone too, so the portable archive shrinks from 123 MB to about 50 MB.

releases.title: The Mac app is built for macOS 11 and later again
releases.summary: Khandaq v0.2.47 for Mac asked for macOS 11 but did not open on macOS 11 to 15: its libraries had been built for macOS 26. This release builds them for macOS 11 and checks every file in the app before packing it. The Windows and Linux builds get the call checks written in August, which had never reached them, and pictures you receive are read with a fixed libexif on Windows and Mac.

changes.title: The Mac app is built for macOS 11 and later
changes.description: v0.2.47 took its libraries from a package manager that builds them for the newest macOS, so on macOS 11 to 15 the app did not open. Every library in the app now targets macOS 11, and the build refuses to pack the app if any file in it needs a newer macOS or loads a library from outside the app. It has been run on macOS 26; on macOS 11 to 15 it is checked file by file, not yet by running it. Profiles and message history from v0.2.47 open as before. The app is still for Macs with Apple Silicon and is still not notarized.

changes.title: Calls on Windows and Linux get the packet checks
changes.description: In August the app got checks on the packets that carry a call: a packet whose header claims more data than it holds is dropped before anything is copied, and so is an audio packet too short to carry any sound. Without them, a contact in a call could send packets that make the app write past the end of a buffer. The Windows and Linux builds compiled an unchanged copy of the network library and never got these checks. They are built from the patched copy now, like the Mac app.

changes.title: Received pictures are read with libexif 0.6.26
changes.description: To show a received photo the right way up, the app reads the camera information inside it with libexif. Up to 0.6.25, libexif could be made to crash, or to leak memory contents, by a picture carrying crafted Fuji or Olympus maker notes (CVE-2026-40386). 0.6.26 fixes that and two related bugs (CVE-2026-32775, CVE-2026-40385).

changes.title: Less of FFmpeg and a newer PCRE2 in the Mac app
changes.description: The Mac app used to carry all of FFmpeg. It now carries only the parts it uses for the camera, voice messages and video calls, with no network access and no filters. Its MP4 reader no longer reads three kinds of boxes a voice message never contains, which have known bugs and no fixed FFmpeg 8.1 release yet (CVE-2026-52297, CVE-2026-96611, CVE-2026-107678). PCRE2 moves to 10.49.

releases.title: The new look on the computer, with requests that wait for your answer
releases.summary: Khandaq for Windows, macOS and Linux gets the look the phones got in v0.2.46: one list with the people online now first, and a conversation that says before you send whether a message goes now or waits in transit. Rebuilding every screen turned up older problems as well, fixed here: the computer accepted every contact request by itself and threw its message away, turning off Keep history lost messages still waiting to be sent, and a profile with a few hundred contacts took half a minute to open.
